initial_presentation: A 6-year-old Chinese girl visited the clinic with complaints of night blindness and progressively worsening vision in both eyes over the past month. There was no history of consanguineous marriage or family history of eye disorders.

A 62-year-old Japanese woman from a non-consanguineous family, whose identical twin sister had shown similar symptoms, presented with gait disturbance. No other family members showed similar disorders. Their mother had died of a malignant tumor at the age of 72, but no significant ataxia or cognitive impairment had been observed until her death. Their father had been healthy until his 90s. The patient had exhibited normal physical and neurological development. At the age of 68 years, she was admitted to a hospital due to dancing-like involuntary movements in the hands and feet. Neurological examination revealed choreic movement, saccadic eye movement, slurred speech, limb and trunk ataxia, and increased deep tendon reflexes in the upper and lower limbs. Babinski sign was negative. No superficial sensory disturbance or Romberg sign was detected. There was no evidence of bladder or rectal disturbance.

A 3-year-old male child with a history of strabismus and cleft lip was referred to our clinics due to an unusual optic disc and visual loss. During the second trimester of pregnancy, the mother developed a generalized maculopapular rash but did not experience headache, fever, conjunctivitis, arthralgia, or myalgia.

An 18-year-old female presented with a one-year history of progressive muscle atrophy and weakness, initially affecting the upper limbs and later involving the lower limbs, leading to difficulty in walking independently. The patient had no significant past medical history and reported the onset of bilateral hearing loss concurrent with the motor symptoms. There was no history of trauma, ototoxic drug usage, loud noise exposure, or similar complaints in her family. Physical examination revealed normal higher mental functions, weakness, and muscle atrophy in both upper and lower limbs. Neurological examination showed decreased muscle tone and bulk, generalized weakness more pronounced in distal muscles, muscle power of 3/5 in both upper and lower limbs, normal superficial reflexes, bilaterally exaggerated deep tendon reflexes, and extensor plantar responses bilaterally. Fasciculations were observed in the tongue and legs.

A 14-year-old female presented with missing or unerupted maxillary anterior teeth. Eight years prior, she experienced trauma to the maxillary anterior region, resulting in the avulsion of several deciduous teeth and fractures of others, which were subsequently extracted. Her medical history was unremarkable, and there was no family history of dental or genetic anomalies. Examination revealed a deficient maxilla on the right side, causing facial asymmetry. In the right maxillary arch, the central incisor, lateral incisor, and canine were missing or unerupted, with the alveolar mucosa in the area enlarged and covered by fibrous tissue. Additionally, there was a rotated first premolar, an erupting second premolar, and unerupted first and second molars on the right side. On the left side of the maxillary arch, only the central incisor was missing, with all other teeth present. In the mandibular arch, all teeth were present except for the third molars, and all teeth exhibited some degree of hypoplasia. Oral hygiene was poor, with an active carious lesion on the mandibular left first molar. There was also deficient maxillary growth on the right side, indicating arch collapse.

A 69-year-old Caucasian male presented with a progressively enlarging, asymptomatic mass in the left submandibular region over a period of 3 months. His medical, family, and psychosocial history were unremarkable, and he had no history of previous surgical treatments. On physical examination, the mass measured 8 × 5 cm, originating from level Ib (submandibular region) and extending into levels III and IV. The mass was adherent to underlying structures and had a soft texture. There was no pain or other symptoms. Examination of the right cervical region, oropharynx, thyroid, and upper respiratory airways showed no abnormalities.

The patient is an 11-year-old boy whom we first evaluated in the endocrine clinic at 8 years of age for obesity. The patient is the male child of nonconsanguineous Guatemalan parents and was born at 41 weeks of gestation by spontaneous vaginal delivery to a 23-year-old, gravida 2, para 1 mother. The pregnancy was not complicated by any exposure to viral infection or medications. His siblings and both parents are healthy with no family history of miscarriages, stillbirths, congenital abnormalities, or learning difficulties.

A 57-year-old man presented with a two-week history of recurrent nausea, lack of appetite, fatigue, and inability to sleep, along with left lower quadrant pain and a feeling of fullness in his mid-abdomen.

A 57-year-old Chinese female presented with irregular postmenopausal vaginal bleeding for 6 months. She has a history of colon cancer and underwent a radical colon cancer operation 20 years ago. The patient and several family members have a history of cancer. Physical examination revealed a small amount of white, odorless vaginal secretions. The cervical surface appeared smooth. The vulva was atrophic, the vagina was patent, and mucosal fold atrophy was noted. The uterus was in an anterior position with a smooth surface and good range of motion. No abnormalities were detected in the bilateral adnexal areas.

A 38-year-old female presented with sudden onset of bilateral blurred vision, followed by a focal headache in the right occipital region one day before admission, which improved with analgesics. The next morning, she experienced a recurrence of blurred vision, predominantly on the left side. She also reported a sudden, severe headache after sneezing, followed by a right-sided headache with a pain score of 3 out of 10, similar to the previous day. Her medical history includes infrequent migraine attacks without aura, a smoking history of 10 pack-years, and receiving the second dose of the Moderna SARS-CoV-2 vaccine 18 days before symptom onset. On admission, a neurological examination revealed a blotchy scotoma in the left eye.
